utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. You have some more questions Mr. Karadzic. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good morning, Excellencies, good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Mladjenovic.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I just have a short question that had to do with this meeting with General Mladic and the others. Did you have any problems regarding abandoned apartments and, if so, how did you resolve that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P1480, could that please be called up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. It was a problem to take care of apartments, but at the very beginning, the civilian police and the military police were given a task. I believe that you have that in the documentation, a form stating that all apartments that were abandoned both by Serbs and Muslims should be sealed off and, from time to time, the police should come and take a look at these apartments and check whether something had happened. At first, that did work, but that was only for a very short time. Practically it was given up then because there was criminal unrest, and it could no longer be controlled. As regards taking care of apartments, houses, buildings, et cetera, you know, Serbs also left. They went to Belgrade and other places. A neighbour would give his neighbour the keys, and people would visit apartments that were next door and houses that were nearby, so that functioned relatively well, at first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 69 in Serbian and in English in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here, we see that Mr. Kovac from Kalinovik is complaining about poor information, poor connections between municipalities, commanding poorly linked up and so on. And then you took the floor. Is that you, the president of the Executive Board?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Production stopped on two occasions due to power outage. Can we have the next page, please. You're asking for Mladic's support here and you're complaining. Can we have the next page. You say that some military personnel are moving into apartments by force. Are those, those abandoned apartments?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And we asked the military component for their help, to have this stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mladjenovic.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as power is concerned, that's true. And not only because of production. At the very beginning, we just had one line of electricity from Visegrad-Gorazde and then when that transmission line fell or, rather, when it was cut off, we practically had no electricity. So, at the very beginning of 1992, or to be more precise, when I went to see the prime minister in Pale around the 24th of May, for instance, and that is the first time I came, Mr. Cancar, a banker, and the director of the public accounting service, we went to ask for a source of assistance in order to have the government help us so that we could build a transmission line from Celebic 23 kilometres long, from Montenegro that is. So it was only in 1994 that our power supply was stabilised. And our production became a bit more intensive in Maglic and other companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who was it that destroyed the transmission line from Gorazde to Foca?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume it was the units that held that area. We -- well, as far as units were concerned, from 1992 onwards, units never left the territory of our municipality. That is to say, towards Gorazde or neighbouring municipalities, irrespective of ethnic background. That is to say, it was the administrative border of the municipality of Foca towards Gorazde and other municipalities like Trnovo and then no one moved from there up until the end of the war. That is to say, until Dayton.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you mentioned that then and now there are two municipalities of Foca. If we take that into account, how many Serbs were there in the Muslim part of Foca during the war?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, I didn't have an opportunity, and I didn't have the ambition to do the accounting. But I know for a while, say, 12 people or several members of a family who were at a farm, Ekonomija, perhaps 3 kilometres away from the town that was the farm of the KP Dom. They worked at that farm and I think they even had some of their offspring there, some of their offspring were born there. After the war, they left, all of them, this entire family. As for these other representatives of the Muslim ethnicity, there was a watch-maker, and in villages, I really don't know, up until 1993, I think, the Cengics, old people were probably protected, and they had friendly relations with Mr. Milosevic and with Mr. Mladic. So they were driven to Belgrade because their son lived in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions of Mr. Mladjenovic at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karadzic. Yes, Mr. Mladjenovic, as you have noted, your evidence in-chief in this case has been admitted, in most part, in writing, that is through your written statement, in lieu of your oral testimony. Now you'll be cross-examined by the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did understand you. In the hotel room, I found the original, the one can be seen with different signatures, different pens, ink. I haven't brought it along, but I had intended to bring it along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, Ms. McKenna.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just to note before I start, I will do my very best to complete within the one hour and 15 minutes that you have allocated for me but I may have to ask your indulgence for a little extra time. But perhaps we can see how we go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let us see. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mladjenovic.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to you, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: We're quite limited in time today, so I'm going to be asking you a series of questions about your statement. I'd appreciate if you could listen carefully and answer as precisely and concisely as possible. I'd like to start with a preliminary point regarding the Foca Territorial Defence. In paragraph 12 of your statement, you state that at the level of the Foca TO staff reservists were issued with weapons, both Muslims and Serbs, as well as the reserve police force. And you also mention Focatrans a number of times in your statement. Now, the Focatrans company had its own Territorial Defence unit, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. As a matter of fact, I doubt that, but I cannot say for sure because the staff of the Territorial Defence was at the level of the municipality, and there was a Chief of Staff, Mr. Sulejman Pilav. His term of office had expired two years before that, the 6th of May. I remember that because that's my patron saint's day. So that was in 1998 before the elections and this -- sorry, let me just finish this sentence. And this went on up until the war conflict itself. So it was him, although Serbs, according to the inter-party agreement, were allocated that post, but it wasn't possible. You have that in the documentation. There was urging of this kind and that, and --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you. Once again I'd just like to remind you to focus very specifically on the question that I'd asked which relates to the Focatrans company.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: If we could please have 65 ter number 24821.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And, Mr. Mladjenovic, I'd just like to clarify this point because it's relevant to both your testimony and the testimony of previous Defence witnesses. This is a document dated the 14th of March, 2013, from the Republika Srpska Ministry of the Interior Criminal Investigation Department to the ICTY, and it states in the first paragraph: "We established that Lazar Kunarac, who was in charge of the documentation of the then TO of Foca including the TO unit Focatrans, was killed in the beginning of the war." And the next paragraph states, if we can have -- oh, excuse me, me it's page 1 in the English as well. An interview was conducted with Momcilo Markovic, who was the commander of the then Territorial Defence unit in Focatrans. It is clear from this document, isn't it, that there was a Territorial Defence unit in the Focatrans company; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. Absolutely not. And it almost seems illogical to me. This entire Territorial Defence was at the level of the municipality, and the staff was at the level of the municipality. So I absolutely cannot assert, there's no way I can do that, that this structure --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Do you accept that this document states --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I'm not aware of that. That is what is written here, but I claim that I was not aware of that situation, nor am I aware of that situation now. And this is a document from 2013. So I did not know about this. I even didn't know that the late gentleman, Mr. Kunarac worked in Focatrans. I didn't even know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honours. First of all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's hear from Ms. McKenna about the basis upon which we can admit this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The witness testified in a number -- mentioned a number of times in his statement the Focatrans company and the suggestion that the Muslims were armed through Focatrans. If you'd bear with me, I can find the reference. And this is a previous -- this is something that we've heard from previous Defence witnesses. I -- we submit that this document impeaches the witness on this point as it proves that there was a Focatrans Territorial Defence unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By Defence witness, who do you refer to?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. It was Witness Pljevaljcic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Whose words is this, that -- that is saying that Foca TO included Focatrans TO unit and Markovic was the commander of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a letter from the Republika Srpska Ministry of Interior Criminal Investigation Department which was sent to the Office of the Prosecutor in response to a request on this specific point. Further to the testimony [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we do not know whose words they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: They're the words of the representative from the criminal investigation department of the present Republika Srpska [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Yes, Mr. -- thank you. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. This has no probative value in contradicting the testimony of this witness because it -- as it -- you picked up from the text it doesn't even say that Mr. Markovic claimed to have been the commander of the Territorial Defence unit. So, for all we know, this inspector of the MUP in 2013 just either made an assumption or we don't know where he got that information. So this isn't the type of contradictory information that would be admissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you like to add anything, Ms. McKenna?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honour, in our submissions, the -- an official document from the -- the Criminal Investigation Department of the Ministry of Interior, in response to a request from the Office of the Prosecutor, stating that an interview was conducted should -- has -- has significant probative value and should be taken on its face.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: But, Ms. McKenna, didn't the witness say, I doubt that, but I cannot say for sure. I cannot say for sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, I don't -- it -- the witness said that he couldn't say for sure whether a -- a Focatrans Territorial Defence unit existed. This document, in our submission, proves that such a unit existed, which is relevant to both this witness's evidence and the previous Defence witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber is of the view it's not appropriate to admit this document through this witness. We'll not admit this at this time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Turning to a completely different topic, Mr. Mladjenovic, at paragraph 16 of your statement, you talk about the SDS rallies in the town stadium in 1990 and 1991. And you state that the messages from our rallies were worded in the spirit of respect for neighbourly relations to preserve peace and to preserve our common country. Now, this Chamber has heard evidence from a Witness KDZ239 that Vojislav Maksimovic, who as you state in your statement was the president of the SDS Deputies Club and was present at the rally in Foca, Mr. Maksimovic at a SDS rally in Gorazde at the end of 1990 stated that in the previous war, blood flowed in the river Drina and now this time blood will flow down both the rivers Drina and Cehotina. And also Witness 33 testified in the Kunarac case that at the SDS founding rally in Foca, it was declared that the river Drina would flow bloody again. Now do you agree that this was not a message that was worded in the spirit of respect for neighbourly relations to preserve peace?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me say straight away that the Serb Democratic Party at the stadium, that is to say, when it was established on the 1st of September, it's true Mr. Maksimovic was there, Mr. Cengic was there, among others, of course, President Karadzic, Plavsic, Koljevic, not to mention everybody now. I do not remember exactly, but I don't believe that Mr. Maksimovic would say that at that gathering, although later it was later, after the elections, that he became president of the SDS club and the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The gathering that you mentioned obviously was held in 1990. It was an electionary [as interpreted] and then in 1991, the Assembly of the trinity was held and all the leaders of the Serbian Democratic Party were there and there was an academician, the late Mr. Raskovic who was present as a guest. So these are two gatherings. One held in 1990 and the other one held in 1991. Not in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously you made a mistake there. As for what was discussed in Gorazde, please, I cannot confirm that, because I did not take part except at those two gatherings that you referred to. And that is correct, two gatherings.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Let's talk about later statements that were made. Witness KDZ239 gave evidence that in early April 1992 there was propaganda on Radio Foca where Miroslav Stanic stated that it was not possible to live with Muslim neighbours anymore, that Serbs couldn't permit themselves to be woken up by the Hodza every morning from the mosque minaret, and that there was a danger of the Serb population or units being circumcised. Now, did you hear these messages from Mr. Stanic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear that. So I did not hear that. I confirm that I did not hear that. But, at any rate, there must be a note or something if that is correct, but I did not hear that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Well, let's look at Mr. Stanic's own words when speaking in an interview on --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stanic?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. When speaking in an interview on the third anniversary of the take-over the Foca, he stated -- and for the parties' reference this is P3476. Mr. Stanic stated: "If certain individuals had been in the command at the beginning of the conflict we would certainly not be sitting here in free Foca and we would probably have a constant headache from the muezzin singing from the tops of the minarets." So, again, I'll ask you, this doesn't suggest a desire to preserve neighbourly relations and peace, does it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. It would not contribute to good relations and peace in Foca, but -- but, roughly, that is three years into the war, if I understood you correctly. That statement can only be confirmed by him. I did not hear it, but, I mean, quite surely, in that context, I could not -- I mean, I didn't understand that that is what was being said at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can understand the beginning of the war but now, no, because he had no one to say this to.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Let's move back to discuss the time prior to the war starting. In paragraph 14 of your statement, you explain that the Serbian municipality of Foca was formed on the 21st of December, 1991. And then in paragraph 20, you state that the Muslims obstructed the work of the Foca Municipal Assembly in many ways, and energy was wasted and that was why the Serbian Municipal Assembly of Foca was formed in December 1991. Now, in fact, Mr. Mladjenovic, the Serb municipality of Foca and its bodies were formed pursuant to instructions given by Mr. Karadzic, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is absolutely not that Mr. Karadzic provided those. Let me explain briefly. When the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina was left by the Serb deputies because they had been outvoted, then definitely alongside the assertions that I perhaps need not remind you of but they were to the effect that Alija Izetbegovic was prepared to sacrifice peace for sovereignty, and so on and so forth. It was then that out of caution we established on the 24th and not on the 21st, or perhaps it may have been the 25th of December, 1991, the Assembly of Foca Municipality. I think it was called the Assembly of Foca Municipality in BiH or something of the sort. In -- so that we be prepared. It all pointed to deteriorating relations and a bad situation. As a matter of fact, I have a flyer that was distributed at a promotional rally in Foca attended by over 100.000 people which is probably the largest SDA rally in Foca --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: MR. Mladjenovic, again I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and they were distributed by Mr. Murat, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Again, I'm going to have to ask you to focus very clearly on the question I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Could we please have P3337.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is correct that ... go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mladjenovic, this is an intercepted conversation between Mr. Stanic and Mr. Karadzic on 6th of January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Could we please have pages 2 in the B/C/S and English versions, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And halfway down the page in the English version, Mr. Stanic says: "We have formed a Serb municipality, and you have that information."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC RESPONDS
utterances.text: "All right." Stanic states: "If this thing should go differently on the 15th we'll have a public promotion."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC RESPONDS
utterances.text: "Yes, yes, and take complete control of your own affairs? And Mr. Stanic responds: "Yes, yes, everything as it is in the instructions." So, Mr. Mladjenovic, according to Mr. Stanic, the formation of the Serb municipality bodies was pursuant to Karadzic's instructions; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the Serb leadership having learned from their previous experience with the municipal -- with the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina suggested as a fallback position to establish the assembly in Foca. It couldn't function in legal terms because the last assembly session with the Muslims, Serbs and Montenegrins and Croats, because there was a Croat among the deputies, was held on the 15th of March, 1992, together. Let me tell you something else.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: -- I'm going to -- I'm sorry. I'm going to interrupt you because I would really like to focus on this issue of the formation and the reasons for the formation of the assembly. Now you, yourself, attended the extended session of the Serbian Democratic Party Main Board and Executive Committee which was held on the 14th of February in Sarajevo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, I'm sorry to interrupt you. But did we hear the witness's answer to your previous question? Mr. Stanisic [sic] said in this intercept that everything is as it is in the instruction. Do you have anything to say about that, Mr. Mladjenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The instructions or recommendations had to do with the establishment of the assembly, which never -- was never operational in 1992 up until the 8th of April. Until then, there was the full municipal assembly of both Muslims and Serbs. Also, the Executive Board as a collective body functioned until the 8th of April as can be seen in various documents, communiques, and statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: So just to clarify this point the instructions to which Mr. Stanic was referring are the instructions received from Mr. Karadzic to set up the Serb Municipal Assembly and the Serb bodies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it is a matter of recommendation rather than instruction. An instruction is something different, as a term, as well as its meaning. I think it was a recommendation. And if one follows up on that recommendation, concludes that the assembly was established on the 25th of December, 1991. I don't think it was the case with the Executive Board though. The conversation you referred to, actually probably refers to an event where I was present at the Main Board of the SDS, and it was done so as to fill in positions by Muslims, which was, later on, actually done.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]... let's --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we ask Ms. McKenna to show us where does it say that this instruction came from me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: That -- that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: She asked the question, and he -- so he confirmed that -- that instruction or recommendation was coming from -- was -- came from the Main Board or Mr. Karadzic. Do you confirm that, Mr. Mladjenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not Karadzic by the Main Board. The Main Board was a collective body. It can make -- reach conclusions and any of the members of the Presidency of that body can sign it. I also managed a collective body when there were sessions. Everyone voted, and then I was the one who signed it. That was the rule.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Well, let's explore this issue of what exactly was formed pursuant to these instructions in a little more detail. We were about to discuss the 14th of February meeting in Sarajevo at the Holiday Inn.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter 11021A.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mladjenovic, as you've just confirmed, you attended this meeting.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And the transcript for this -- Mr. Mladjenovic, this is a transcript of your statement at this meeting. The transcript should be attached. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: If we could please play the audio.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "I'm speaking on behalf of the Serbian executive committee of Foca and that other one, that is slowly dying. I do not wish to participate in the debate here but I would like to ask some questions that I would like to find answers to. That is, I, as a representative of the people in Foca municipality. Serbian people in Foca municipality. Considering the fact that we did everything that the centre had requested us to do and considering the instructions we received in this field when setting up the Serbian Assembly and Executive Committee, we got far ahead with the work of the Executive Committee for a simple reason at least with some operational issues by which we wish to finally round up the Serbian territory of Foca municipality within the Serbian autonomous region of Herzegovina. Of course, we wouldn't think of resolving the Serbian territory in Bosnia-Herzegovina partially. For these reasons, I find it necessary to, first of all, establish Serbian municipalities regardless of the borders of existing municipalities. This is the case with us, and we will not have any regard for that."

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mladjenovic, can you confirm that this was you speaking?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: So in this statement, you explicitly emphasise to your colleagues at the SDS that when setting up both the Serbian Assembly and the Executive Committee, you did everything that the centre requested you to do, considering the instructions that you received; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think the Executive Board was complete, but the assembly was. Complete in terms of composition.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but just to clarify my question, you -- you formed the -- regardless of whether they were complete in their composition at that point, the assembly and the Executive Committee were formed pursuant to the instructions that you received from Dr. Karadzic and the SDS Main Board; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the Main Board. I don't recall -- well, perhaps it was signed by Karadzic, but I don't think he did because there was no order with any signatures. It was simply an instruction to react out of caution, and it was not applied until the 8th of April, 1992. So a meeting with the Muslims was set up in the same composition of the Executive Board as it functioned before the war. You can see that from the conclusions. There are documents to support that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we will receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6264, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, can I ask the following: Is the entire transcript of the 14th of February meeting admitted? It was a Plenary not the Main Board.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, not all of it was read out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If necessary, you may tender it later on. But we'll admit this part at the moment. But I don't follow the -- page 3 of this transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's an additional excerpt which we won't be using, so my colleague, Mr. Reid, will simply upload the excerpt of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The two pages.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Exactly. Thank you for pointing that out.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Now I'm going to move on to a different topic, Mr. Mladjenovic. In paragraph 20 of your statement, you discuss the formation of the Crisis Staff on the 3rd of April, 1992, and you state that the local para state and para military factions had stronger influence than the republican commissioner and the local authorities headed by you. And, again, in paragraph 25, you discuss the -- how difficult it was in the circumstances to control the situation which was bordering on anarchy. I would like to explore the issue of who was in control or authority in Foca at the time. Now, the Crisis Staff led the Serb take-over of the Foca municipality, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff -- please, if I may say just a few things that seem to have been bundled up together without any order. You understand that I'd like to have that in sequence in terms of dates and order. It is true that the Crisis Staff on the Serbian side was established on the 3rd of April, 1992. It is true that, as per function of the Executive Board, as a collective organ, I was the third person on the list. There was the president of the party and president of the municipality, Mr. Milicic, and then it was me, and so on and so forth. As regards that body I have to point out, yet again, joint work until the 8th of April in the afternoon took place with members of the Executive Board of both structures, Muslim and Serb, as you can see in the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: May I just interrupt you. Your evidence on this is on the record in your statement. Now I'm asking about specific aspects of the take-over. I'd like you to focus on the aspects that I'm asking you. My question is: In respect of the Serb take-over of Foca, the armed take-over, that was led by the Crisis Staff, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The take-over the power took place, because you mention paramilitary structures and unrest and so on and so forth, and, indeed, I mention it in the statement. But the Crisis Staff reacted after I was actually at the municipal building with four of my associates. That was myself, Mr. Lakovic Jedhen [phoen], who was the head of the Ministry of Defence, and Dzemal Aganovic [phoen]. We returned to invest another effort on the afternoon -- in the afternoon of the 8th of April to try and save the situation so that, in addition to the communique that I signed alongside Mr. Taib that people should not leave their apartments and move about in the streets, and so on and so forth. However, on the 8th, it was not possible, and it is not true that we took over, or the Crisis Staff, Serbian Crisis Staff, took over Foca, because only as of the 9th on, there was combat in Alaca [phoen] which is deep inside the territory, upstream the Cehotina river. So Foca was not taken over in five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: But again -- it wasn't. I'm not contending that it was, Mr. Mladjenovic. But, again, I'm going to read the statement of Mr. Stanic, who was the president of the Crisis Staff, to you. And again this is from the interview that I mentioned previously. Mr. Stanic states, and this, again, is P3476 for the parties' reference: "I was the commander on behalf of the SDS which enabled me to become the first war commander." He states: "We liberated the town in six days. By the 25th of April, we managed to liberate the whole of Foca municipality, the largest municipality in Republika Srpska. I submitted my war report to the ministerial counsel, as it was then called at the time, at the beginning of June. We were active in the Crisis Staff and later in the army command." So now, according to Crisis Staff president Stanic, the Crisis Staff, under his authority, led the take-over. So does Mr. Stanic's statement refresh your recollection on this point?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have to, and logically speaking, it didn't happen that we went to Radio Stara Herzegovina or Radio Foca to issue announcements. Again, it was done by a collective organ. I need to say, though, that I definitely worked not in order to justify - I have to say that - but as of the 3rd, as of the date of establishment, I was active in the Executive Board until the 8th. On the 19th of April, I basically returned to the municipality and began setting up civilian authorities. I had inherited three members, and we needed to find another three who were Serbs. That it true.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm -- again, we're focussing on the specific -- the role of -- the issue of the take-over of the municipality. We'll come onto the civilian authorities in a moment. But just to go back to your statement, in paragraph 30, you state that - and this, again, is during the negotiations - on the 8th of April, you went to the Serb Crisis Staff headquarters in Cerezluk to receive the demands that you were to give to the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And you state a minister in the BH government and president of the Crisis Staff dictated these requests. Now this reference to the minister is a reference to Velibor Ostojic, who was the minister of information in the Republika Srpska government; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And you stated that communications for the first two or three days when Mr. Ostojic was in Foca were possible. Just to clarify, Mr. Ostojic was present during the take-over of Foca, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not until the end. Not all the way up to the end. I can't guess or estimate because he received information that a government was being set up in Pale and he was supposed to go there. As dictated by logic, he had to resume his work as the then-minister of information in the joint government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. So he withdrew and left us to the commissioners and to us to do the best we could because we had not had any previous war time experience. We had to go on our intuition and knowledge that we had obtained in the previous organs or structures.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: I want to focus right now on the -- the issue of whether Mr. Ostojic was present in Foca during the take-over. You've said that he was not there until the end, but he was there at the beginning of the take-over; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second. Yesterday I stated here that through activities of joint forces of Gradska and Foca definitely in late September and up until the 10th of October, the territory of Foca was finally determined, administratively speaking. We stopped at those borders and nothing moved until the Dayton accords. Our units did not go out to Foca or out of the municipality of Foca to the neighbouring municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, my -- my question relates to when Velibor Ostojic was present in Foca. Now, there is a report from Mr. Foca [sic] in evidence before the trial that's P -- excuse me, from Ostojic. That's P3338. And it's a report from Foca on Belgrade Radio dated 14th of April, 1992, where he states: "The Serbian Territorial Defence is controlling a huge part of the town. The entire Serb Territorial Defence in the Foca commune is on its feet." So, again, I'll ask you to confirm that Mr. Ostojic was present during the Serb take-over of Foca; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was definitely not there. If you believe that the take-over took place on the 19th, when civilian authorities basically started functioning. When I returned to the municipality with my associates, I think he left Foca before that. I think he was there on the 7th or 8th. He was definitely there then. As for what you mentioned, the 16th Company, I didn't have time to tell Varac Ekmen [phoen], a member of the Municipal Board, to tell anything because shooting had started. I simply gave that paper to him and, indeed, he replied, saying we had to have known. And I didn't even really go to the gist of it, to tell you the truth, because minutes under such circumstances are like years.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, I'm focussing right now on the issue of who was in control during the take-over.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter number 40609A, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mladjenovic, this is a video with Mr. Ostojic and it's an interview with a BBC journalist 18 months after the conflict broke out in Foca. I'd just like you to listen to what he says about the Foca take-over.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: If we could play the video, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: "... people who were running in the town in the spring and summer of last year? "People we have talked to say that you were clearly one of the people who were running the town in the spring and summer of last year. "No. Foca was run by the Crisis Staff. I was in Foca for a certain period of time only as I was in other parts of the republic. My task was to preserve property and establish civilian authority in all parts of Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: So, Mr. Mladjenovic, according to Mr. Ostojic, he was in Foca to help establish civilian authority. Is that consistent with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I don't read what Mr. Ostojic said that way. He said he was in Foca for a certain period of time as he was in other parts of the republic. And then he said that his task was to preserve property and establish civilian authority in all parts of Republika Srpska. So I don't think that's a very fair question given the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In any event, the transcript doesn't seem to be correct. Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the transcript, Excellency? Let's see how this was translated.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we have a number for the entire transcript. There are a lot of redacted places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Why don't we play it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: If we play it again, I think that should clarify matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: "... that you were clearly one of the people who were running the town in the spring and summer of last year "People we have talked to, the refugees, say that you were clearly one of the people who were running the town in the -- "No, Foca was run by the Crisis Staff. I was in Foca for a certain period of time only as I was in other parts of republic for a certain period of time. My task was to preserve property and to establish civilian authority in all parts of Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And what is your question, Ms. McKenna?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: My question was that -- well, as according to Mr. Ostojic, he was in Foca to help establish civilian authority, and -- is that consistent with your recollection? As ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, my objection was that this mischaracterises what was said by Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: I don't read it as a mischaracterisation, but I can rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, Mr. Ostojic says that his task was to establish civilian authority in all parts of the Republika Srpska. Do you accept that he was in Foca to establish -- to help establish civilian authority?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm more prone to believing that closer to the truth is the fact that he was in that area because his mother lived there. He just happened to be there. And then he could not return either to Pale or to Sarajevo, in particular. I believe that his intentions were good. But when I returned a couple of days later, perhaps on the 22nd or 23rd, or thereabouts, he told me that we, members of the Executive Board, were dragging our feet and then he -- and then he concluded that he was in our way. We admitted that that was the fact, and then he left to Pale. And then, from time to time, he would return. He returned to Pale and -- he basically got out of our hair and let us do what we could.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Well, according to Mr. Ostojic, Foca was run by the Crisis Staff. Is that consistent with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the early days, there was a Crisis Staff, and there was the staff of the Territorial Defence of the Serbian army. That's what it was called. These were the roots of the creation of more organised units. Only after the election of President Karadzic on 12th of May was the military established at that same assembly session which was probably in Banja Luka, but I'm not sure. Then the situation improved. The situation in the military improved. The military was a very serious structure. It lacked inorganisation [as interpreted] in terms of formations and it lacked in personnel, of course. And then the officers who had served in the JNA returned because they hailed from the municipality of Foca, and then the military started being more organised, and it started being organised into military units.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: But you agree that in the early days, the Crisis Staff was the authority in the town.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps some of the component affiliated with the army and the TO staff. And this certainly didn't interfere. Maybe they overlapped with the civilian issues that were topical at the time. In other words, that situation imposed the tasks of the Crisis Staff which you can see in the published documents. You can see that the Crisis Staff stopped working at the moment when conditions were in place for the municipal assembly to start functioning. Then the conclusions and decisions would be taken over and approved by the assembly itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll come onto that stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we ask for the number of the integral transcript because we may want to use parts thereof once we see what has been redacted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Certainly we'll forward it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, could you expand on the reason why you're objecting to the admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Actually, I said we had no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. My fault. We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6265, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Just finally on this topic of law and order at that time, Mr. Ostojic said in -- actually, could we have P4986, please. So, Mr. Mladjenovic, this is a report dated the 30th of April, 1992, from Velibor Ostojic to the Republika Srpska government providing information on the achievements of the Serb Territorial Defence in the Foca area. And it's stated that the Foca Serb TO has been cleaning up the Foca area and has liberated the Ustikolina area. And in the final paragraph it states: "Situation in the liberated areas is stabilising because of the rule of law and because the institutions of civilian authority have control over the overall situation." So, in fact, the local authorities had a significant degree of control over what was going on in Foca, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to brag, but let it be the way you put it. We tried to have the civilian authorities functioning and dealing with all the issues. At that time, a significant number - and I repeat, a significant number - of the Muslims were in the city.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said -- didn't say, "I don't want to brag." He said that he bragged, that Mr. Ostojic bragged, that he was trying to take a more credit and that was due to him. That's on line 25, page 27.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you confirm that, Mr. Mladjenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Prosecutor, I would be much happier if the situation was as described in here. But I am afraid that Mr. Ostojic, who was minister at the time, bragged a little. It was not all a bad -- a bed of roses, you know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's come on to the issue of the Serb forces that were present in Foca. Now, at paragraphs 42 to 44 of your statement, you discuss at some length the Serb forces who were in Foca at the start of the conflict. You speak about one group of men commanded by a Lainovic, one group of men known colloquially as the Belgrade Battalion who came around --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lainovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: So there was Lainovic's men. There was a group of men you referred to as the Belgrade Battalion who came around 15th of May and withdrew at the same time as the JNA and there were other officers operating as part of the Serbian TO forces until their withdrawal with the JNA in May 1992. Now, in your discussion of Serb forces during the take-over, it's strange that there's no mention of the officers operating as part of the Serb forces who remained in Foca after the JNA left --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. McKenna, I apologise. Chamber needs to rise at this moment. We'll have a break for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. McKenna. I apologise again for the interruption. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, we were just coming onto discuss the Serb forces that remained in the Foca area after the JNA withdrawal. Now, the civilian authorities in Foca closely liaised with the military authorities in pursuit of their shared goals, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to correct you straight away. Military formations and paramilitaries that appeared at the very beginning of the war in Foca -- on the 15th of May, the Army of Republika Srpska was officially set up, and they withdrew. It was not a battalion. There were some 60 men or so. That's we called them, because the locals who hailed from Belgrade and Foca -- and, for that reason, that's what we called them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you. And we're going to come on to discuss those soldiers who remained in Foca. But I would just like to ask you to confirm that the civilian authorities and the military authorities liaised closely.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only to the extent necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter number 24897.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mladjenovic, you'll see that this is a document dated 17th of September, 1992, and it's an appointment by Mr. Karadzic of members of the War Commission. And it lists Mr. Stanic, Marko Kovac, yourself, and Nedo Radovic. Now, just to confirm, Marko Kovac was the commander of the Tactical Group Foca; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: So this is Mr. Stanic, yourself, and yourself on a commission with Commander Kovac suggests a close liaison between you, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you straight away. I've not seen this paper before. Ever. I suppose that I was in that group because of supplies and logistic support. I liaised with companies to make sure that they received salaries. That was my role. I have not seen this paper before. And that commission or whatever body that was, that was the only manner in which I could be engaged in it. And let me tell you also that on the 17th of September, 1992, the Crisis Staff had long stopped working when the regular Army of Republika Srpska was set up, and that was on the 12th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you. We're discussing the co-operation between the civilian authorities, that's you, and the military authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6266, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Now, on the same date as you were appointed to this commission, you attended the meeting with Mladic that you just spoke about earlier in your testimony today. If we could have P1480, please. While the document is coming up, Mr. Mladjenovic, other attendees of this meeting, included the Tactical Group Foca commander Kovac, Mr. Stanic, Mr. Maksimovic, and the Foca Municipal Assembly president, Milicic. I'm interested in page 66 of the document, when we have it. So you'll see here a statement by Mr. Stanic, who is head of the War Presidency, and he states that until the 2nd of June, 1992, he was troops commander. And he goes on: "The population of Foca, before the war, was 42.000, of which number around 51 per cent were Muslims, and 49 per cent Serbs and Montenegrins. Now the percentage of Serbs in Foca is 99 per cent." States they can receive 5.000 refugees and the civilian government is functioning. So this update by Mr. Stanic to Mr. Mladic, in the presence of these other military and civilian authorities, suggests a close liaison between those authorities, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It existed to the extend needed. As far as the civilian authorities are concerned, they were concerned with logistics, the supply of food, clothes, footwear, and the salaries. And I suppose that both Milicic and I appeared in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's talk about who the military forces were. At paragraph 52 of your statement, you say that - with reference to adjudicated fact number 797 - that the house at the address Osmana Djikica 16 was never the headquarters or housed any units of the regular army at that time. Now, it's on the record before this Chamber that, among those who lived at that address, were members of the group led by Dragoljub Kunarac. That for the parties' reference is adjudicated fact 797 and 799. Kunarac was known as Zaga; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that he was known by his nickname, but I claim categorically that he -- there was never a military staff there. He didn't have a military staff. He acted together with a few people in the early days of the war, and those units were outside of regular units. And when it comes to the staff, the staff of the tactical group or the military command was 3 kilometres away from Foca, east of Foca, in the former women's prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was used for any other purposes, but it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Is it your position that the unit led by Zaga was not part of the Tactical Group Foca?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at first. I believe that they were subjected to destructive activities and inflicted a lot of harm to the Serbian citizens of Foca and all the other honest people of Foca. So their activities were detrimental to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Could we please have P3354.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mladjenovic, this is an order from the commander of the Foca Tactical Group. And it's dated the 7th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Could we -- and if we go to the last page --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: You'll see that it's signed by Commander Marko Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Now could we please have page 4 of the B/C/S and page 3 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And I'd like to focus your attention under the heading command post Ustikolina. And the second bullet point it states: "The independent Zaga detachment shall take part in mopping up settled areas in the direction of the 5th Battalion's attack."

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's bullet point 3, right? Bullet point 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: So this document, according to this document, the unit led by Zaga was part of the Tactical Group Foca; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't agree with that. At the beginning of the war, I believe that he had worked in Montenegro, and then he arrived. And after the 12th most certainly because this date followed the setting up of the tactical group and the consolidation of the army, so after the 12th of May, you can check that. After the 12th of May. Then it was possibly involved or his unit became a part or acted in concert with the regular units of the Army of Republika Srpska but not at the very beginning, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And so Kunarac and his men who committed systematic rapes and abuse at Osmana Djikica 16 and other locations in and around Foca were part of tactical group Foca which was a part of the regular armed forces at the time.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of that happened in the month of April. I just associated that that facility was not used for the unit command but for other purposes. Maybe you will recall that that's exactly what I stated for something that was detrimental and stirred the humanity, i.e., contributed to a phase of uninterrupted hatred and against the Serbian population with regard to what they did. And I stated what I thought about that, and I honestly and deeply apologise to the victims who were treated in that way, and I sincerely sympathise with them. And I also have to say that I have a need at one moment not to justify anything but to present a fact, if you allow me, in a closed session, of course. Perhaps it may benefit somebody and particularly the Prosecutor and the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: I suggest that if Mr. Karadzic wants to pursue this issue he will do it in his re-examination, but right now I'd like to focus on the -- my questions.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And you have stated that these abused happened in the month of April. The Trial Chamber has heard evidence that at the partisan sports hall at Foca high school in the Buk Bijela huts in Karaman's house in Miljevina and in other detentions in and around Foca throughout 1991 -- sorry, excuse me, 1992, many Muslim women were subjected to repeated rapes by multiple perpetrators. And one witness, KDZ216 stated that it was generally known that soldiers were -- stated in regard to the women at the partisan sports hall: "It was generally known that soldiers were coming and taking them away and forces them to have sexual relations with them." Now, in your statement, you, at paragraph 49, you state the perpetrators were processed and punished. Firstly let's talk about the protection that was afforded to the women by the Foca authorities in these detention centres. It is on the record before this Chamber that the chief of police and the member -- and a member of the Foca Crisis Staff, Dragan Gagovic, to whom you refer in your statement, was one of the men who came to Kalinovik school, Foca high school, and partisan sports hall and take women out and rape them. And that's adjudicated fact 814. Were you aware of Mr. Gagovic's participation in the rapes?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely not. I would be disappointed, although we're talking about a deceased man, I would be very disappointed if he took part in that. Let tell you straight away that I cannot believe that in view of the personality involved. This person was involved in protection and other forms of co-operation. Old women, children, old men who were in the territory of the municipality of Foca for a while. As for partisan, I mean, there were certain police structures. I mean, there was guard duty. However, pathological persons and persons who got hold of weapons, they were all armed, it was hard to stand up to these bullies and --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Well, let's -- let's talk about the identity of some of these pathological persons who were involved. Pero Elez was identified by KDZ216 as the commander of the soldiers in Karremans house. He decided which soldiers would be given to which girls. And the reference for what is P69, page 43, and P90, page 10. Secondly, Gojko Jankovic was in charge of the detention centre at Buk Bijela where women from the village of Trosanj were taken and multiple rapes were perpetrated. And that reference is P90 and pages 7 and 14 and adjudicated fact 2407. Now Gojko Jankovic was convicted by the Court of BiH in 2007 for his role in the attacks on Foca's non-Serb civilian population. Brane Cosovic commanded the military unit to which Radomir Kovac and Zoran Vukovic belonged. And again that's KDZ216, P69, page 73, and both Kovac and Vukovic were convicted of rape by this Tribunal, not by any court in Foca. Now, these three individuals, Elez, Jankovic and Cosovic, were all praised by Stanic for their achievements in the liberation of Foca, in his interview that we have referred to previously. That's at P6081 for the parties' reference. So, in fact, the perpetrators were not punished by the civilian and military authority, were they?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could not have been punished. As for praise to these individuals by Mr. Stanic, that is his private view. I would absolutely disagree. Perhaps they were combatants, good combatants, but as for the crimes they were charged with before this Tribunal and for which they were punished there is absolutely no justification and I sincerely regret the fact that this happened. And I believe that all persons of integrity in Foca also regret because of this stain on the reputation of Foca.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Well, let's see how the authorities dealt with another one of the rapist. Radovan Stankovic was convicted by the court of BiH in 2006 for rapes and abuse committed at Karaman's house. Were you aware of this conviction?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And he served his sentence at the KPZ Foca and by way of a manoeuvre, obviously there was some lack of attention, and he managed to escape.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And again, again -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter number 23625.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Now this is an order dated 7th of April, 1995, from President Karadzic to the VRS Main Staff to transfer a group of conscripts from the VRS to the Ministry of Interior in order to form a detachment of special police forces in Srbinje? And if we could go to page 2 of this document in both versions. You'll see that entry number one is Radovan Stankovic, detachment commander. So, again, this shows that, rather than being processed and punished as you contend in your statement, Stankovic remained within the VRS; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to tell you that Mr. Karadzic acted probably - most probably - on someone's proposal because he absolutely did not know Radovan Stankovic, I think, and he had no reason to know him. Then someone from the military structure either knew of what he did during the first years of the war - well, that I don't know - but it is quite certain that, had Mr. Karadzic known, he would have eliminated him, 100 percent. And many other proposals that had come from Foca. Believe me, I don't know who proposed him unless there's a signature after that proposal. I assume there is a signature?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mladjenovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6267, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: I'd like to return briefly to the issue of the village of Trosanj. You described your role in negotiating the agreement of 24th April 1992 between the people of Trosanj and the government of Foca representatives and the contents of that agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Could we please have D3316.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document is a familiar one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: It's your signature on this agreement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And at paragraph 5 of the agreement, it states that: "All inhabitants of the village of Trosanj of Muslim ethnicity who surrender their weapons shall be guaranteed all the rights and freedoms stipulated by the constitution of the Serb republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina which includes the security of their lives, their families' lives, and of their property." Now statements were made to the OTP by villagers from Trosanj that the weapons were, indeed, handed in, and receipts were given for this hand-over. And Witnesses 75 and 96 in the Kunarac case testified to that effect. And yet were you aware of this happening?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you explain this to me? What is it that was happening? I know that I was in my office. Three men came. And the head of a company or a battalion - I'm not quite sure - came, escorted by them, and we talked about what could be done in order not to wage war and to spare property. Please --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you. Were you aware that weapons were, in fact, handed in by Muslims and receipts given to them by the Serb authorities for those weapons pursuant to this agreement?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Let me say that straight away, but may I just draw your attention to paragraph 2, the hand-over of weapons of all Serbs who are not involved in military units. And also that weapons will be taken over along with receipts, and so on. I already said in my statement that perhaps I did not get return information. Do read that. That was truthful, but what was said was that they had started bearing weapons, and so on, and then this agreement was not observed. So I did talk to people with the best of intentions. I even talked to Jelec, the representative. Although an influential person from Miljevac talked to Jelec, too, a person I knew myself, and somebody who was involved in trade.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, as I stated, the previous Trial Chambers have heard evidence that weapons were, in fact, handed in. And yet despite this fact, on the 3rd of July, the village was surrounded and attacked by Serb soldiers. And, again, Gojko Jankovic, a man praised by Stanic, was involved in this attack. That's adjudicated fact 2398. Now, during this attack, villagers were -- civilian villagers were brutally beaten and some were killed. And today you say -- and excuse me, and women were taken from -- civilian villagers -- civilian women were taken from the village of Trosanj into detentions at the workers's huts in Buk Bijela where many were raped repeatedly. Now, in your statement you say that you may not have been properly informed by your side of the events of Trosanj. But were you aware that civilians were brutally beaten and killed in the Serb attack on the village?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to tell you quite sincerely that after this talk and this written trail, I did not contact people so that was this obligation on the part of the military component to check this, to take weapons from Serbs and Muslims and to return weapons when the conditions were right. That is what is written there, and that's why I signed this paper. I was counting on seriousness. I left open the possibility that perhaps my side, the military, had not come back to me on this, whether this was being buried or not. Unfortunately, I did not have an opportunity for seeing -- of seeing this myself. And that was the case with Jelec, too. A bit modified --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am aware I'm over time. I would like to move on to the final topic which is the KP Dom, with your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How long would that take?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: 15 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: I'm very grateful, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, in paragraph 48 of your statement, you state that the KP Dom became a military prison in war time. And you state that the civilian authorities' relationship with the KP Dom was minor. The Trial Chamber has heard evidence that the detainees at KP Dom were civilians. And these detainees included civilians brought from Livade, which you mention in your statement, at paragraph 36. And for the parties' reference, I'm referring to KDZ239's testimony at T 18915. And this witness stated: "They took us prisoner at our places of work in the streets, in our homes. Some people were hiding in the woods. And they found them there and brought them to the KP Dom. At any rate, no was one there who had been at the front line." So it's not correct, is it, that as you contend in your statements only perpetrators of violations of military rules and crime were held in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you straight away that I did not even have time to say yes or no to you; but I want to tell you, as far as the KP Dom is concerned, it became a military prison, having been an civilian prison beforehand, but chronologically I would like to go back to that. Indeed, some persons, some Muslims, were brought from Livade, three physicians included. I think that they were in the area of the separation line on that day by the health centre. Dr. Avdo Sadinlija is somebody I knew personally. We were friends from the tennis club, and so on. He was brought in. As far as I found out, Dr. Asima Pilav and Ibrahim Karovic, who headed the SDA list for Foca for the BH National Assembly. I'm not saying there weren't any Serbs; I'm just not sure. They stayed for a few days and they were released. They were allowed to go home. Whereas Dr. Avdo Sadinlija was exchanged because he had an influential brother and probably other relatives, so he was exchanged for a professor of the medical faculty of Sarajevo, Milutin Najdanovic. I think that originally he had come from Nis but he was monstrously killed in Sarajevo after the exchange. I think he was even a member of parliament, but I'm not sure. So that's the package of -- or, rather, it's the fate of these persons. I do apologise. That's how it was. As far as the KP Dom is concerned, it is correct that on the 15th of April, at an ad hoc meeting, but -- well, so when the command was at the school, on the 15th of April, 1992, we appointed Mr. Krnojelac as acting warden of the KP Dom when nobody --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you. We will come on to the appointment of Mr. Krnojelac. I just want to focus --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the chronology of events. And you go ahead and ask.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to focus on the fact that civilians were detained at the KP Dom. Now, at paragraph 31 of your statement, you mention a large number of refugees who had fled to Montenegro. The Trial Chamber has heard evidence from a Muslim refugee who, together with other Muslim refugees, was arrested in Montenegro on the 21st of May, 1992, by a senior police officer from Foca and transferred back to the KP Dom where he was detained for 29 months and 16 days. And that's KDZ017; P3567, pages 7 to 16. Mr. Mladjenovic, were you aware that civilians who had left Foca were being brought back by Foca police and detained in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the Office of the Prosecutor of Montenegro dealt with some of the people who took part in that. That means that they were prosecuted and convicted. As for the day of appointment of Mr. Krnojelac, not a single detainee was at the KP Dom. That happened later. Let me tell you straight away. Indeed, there was withdrawal involved, but it was the Muslim units that were first to arrive at the KP Dom because they had inhabited Donje Polje, that's what it's called. This is the local terrain there. After that, it was used as a military prison and the military command, or rather, the army, absolutely totally had its disposal, the security and everything, except that civilian structures provided food for humanitarian reasons and also --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- soap and detergents and things likes that. Well, not to discuss it at great length.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Let's discuss then in greater detail the involvement of the civilian authorities in the KP Dom. There is a request dated 8th of May, 1992, from Mr. Stanic as the commander of the TG Foca to the KP Dom for the allocation of rooms within the compound for the accommodation of prisoners of war. That's P3341. And then on a decision from Mr. Krnojelac pursuant to this request, allocating the premises of the KP Dom for the accommodation of prisoners of war and detainees, and that's P3342. So in fact the KP Dom was set up as a detention centre on the instructions of Crisis Staff President Stanic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, or, rather, I claim that this was a military prison. And as for the further treatment, in terms of judicial processes and how it was treated, believe me, I don't know. But certainly the army was in charge. They brought people in. They took them for exchanges. It was only the military factor. As for this correspondence between Mr. Stanic and Mr. Krnojelac believe me, I don't know. I didn't have to know about this. But do believe me that I don't know what kind of rooms he asked for. Probably for putting up these person who were being brought in.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: You acknowledge that civilian authorities appointed Mr. Krnojelac as warden of the KP Dom, but you were also actively involved in the appointment and engagement of KP Dom employees, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I mean, for Mr. Krnojelac, yes, and I'm not challenging that at all. He was appointed. This area was not inhabited. Not a single person had been brought in when he was appointed. This was done in order to protect this property that was vast.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a exemplary person, a mathematics teacher, and reserve captain, and that was it. Well, we didn't know --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, we're very limited in time. I'm going to move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Could we please see P3340.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: So this is a decision of 26th of April, 1992, signed by you, in your capacity as president of the Executive Board, allowing the Foca penal and correction facility - that's the KP Dom - to introduce the work obligation for people who are able to work and not engaged in the VJ. So you, on behalf of the Crisis Staff, approved the engagement of certain workers in the KP Dom under obligation; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This has to do with the guard service or, rather, the security service. Because I assume that Krnojelac had asked. And then we agreed to provide persons for work obligation, people who were capable of work. Muslims, perhaps, did not appear in the army in 1991 and 1992, so it had to do with Serbs who were supposed to guard the premises. Because, of course, Krnojelac himself could not have guarded the entire property. Very often, these were retirees, employees of the KP Dom or other persons like policemen who were outside or, rather, who had worked before within the security service there. Either on the premises or outside.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please have 65 ter number 8479. Now we've seen how you were involved in the appointment of the guards for the KP Dom. This --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is all the personnel that was there before or after people were being brought in or before things were moved under military control. That's why.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: This is a request, Mr. Mladjenovic, from KP Dom warden Krnojelac to the Crisis Staff, dated 20th of May, 1992. And he says: "We hereby request the appointment of authorised persons for questioning and examination of captured persons who have been brought to the penal and correctional facility Foca." So the Crisis Staff approval was also required for the appointment of interrogators at the KP Dom; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so. I suppose so. But these were military security officers, as well as some MUP inspectors.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: May I tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we will receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6268, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
