utterances.text: If I may, it is unclear to me at this stage what this leaflet is. But it seems to be linked to -- and purportedly the SDA rally that's outside the scope of the cross-examination. The cross-examination dealt solely with the SDS rally and statements that were made during it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Would you like to respond?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The witness was asked. And he tried to show this leaflet in responding to that question. The Prosecutor didn't want him to do that. I suppose that they were waiting for me to do it in my re-direct; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you point us the relevant part of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me see if I noted that during the cross-examination. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it true this leaflet is related [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The leaflet, on page 12, page 12 of the today's transcript. A question was put to the witness. He tried to say something about the leaflet, but he could not. Line 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We will allow the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, how does this leaflet which was distributed among the 100.000 people reflect on the mindset of the Serbian community in Foca?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only this leaflet. But before bullet point 1, could you please read the content of the text in this leaflet?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters in the booth cannot do sight translation especially if the witness is reading very fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It is impossible for the interpreters to follow.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will read the first sentence slowly: "It is clear that we can no longer live calmly with the Serbs and that the crisis that we are now experiencing will not be resolved for long as a single Serb remains living in our republic. That's why we have to do everything in our power to get rid of them in the most efficient and fastest way. Before we use the last argument which is weapons, we will try and use some more subtle weapons or methods to remove imposters from our country." Mr. Mladjenovic do you know who Senad Sahinpasic, Saja, is? Was he the owner of a newspaper "Vox" and what is the link between this leaflet and "Vox."

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are thinking along the same line. I am sorry you didn't read the next sentence where it says that we were dirty and ugly. Mr. Sahinpasic was an MP in the National Assembly. I now him as my fellow citizen. He is a poet. He puts together verses and is the author of that infamous verse that was uttered in the National Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina when he said there is a duck swimming, there is a goose swimming, and this country will be Turkey eventually. And with or without that the emotions were running very high because for 413 years, not minutes but years, Turkey ruled the area of Bosnia, Serbia and other countries in the Balkan peninsula.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The name on line 23 is Senad Sahinpasic, Saja. On line 25 the witness didn't say that we were thinking along the same lines. He said that this leaflet and newspaper "Vox" were on the same line, and said Sahinpasic was its publisher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a newspaper that was printed in order to add fuel to the hatred and to orchestrate the Sharia laws and regulations. I'm sure that you had the examples of those and you were privy to them, and I'm sure that you will know that what I'm say something very honest and very fair.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On line 8, it should read "Sharia law," and that has not been recorded. Excellencies, I'm tendering this leaflet for admission. I would like it to be marked for identification, and when we have dealt with that, I will have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we leave the leaflet on the ELMO? Yes. Who is -- who was it that got this leaflet or flyer? Is it the Defence or the witness? Mr. Mladjenovic, is it you that got this flyer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a book, which holds the gist of it and quotes the text distributed by Sabanovic. I think it was in circulation because it was distributed at this rally of 100.000 people and they couldn't tell Serbs from Muslims, and they were distributed by Sabanovic and his group. Of course, it ended up in the hands of Serbs and it was very much in circulation. That is how he stirred unrest among Serbs, especially where he says we've lived long with the Serbs. We have become familiar with them. We have strengthened our hatred towards them because they are dirty and ugly, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please concentrate on the answer. So what we are seeing now is part of a book, published by a Serb.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Can I hear from you, Ms. McKenna.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's -- I don't think the provenance of this document is clear at all. We don't know who published it. We don't know when it was published. I think the standards for admissibility are clearly not met.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did you get by this flyer and the book? Who published it and is there an original anywhere?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I can say with credibility that there is the original leaflet. The book was written by Velimir Djurovic. It is called "Lies, Hatred, the Crime."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: For you, Excellencies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you have it in that book with some other words uttered by Ivo Andric, some journalists and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before having seen this in the book, were you aware that it had existed before, that there was the original somewhere?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA MLADJENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw it dozens of times, and I didn't need the book for that. You could easily find it, and I have one even. And I'm surprised I did not offer it to counsel. That is to say, to those who were proofing me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll marked for identification until this Chamber is satisfied with its provenance. And when we -- until we have the English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D3320, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then that concludes your evidence, Mr. Mladjenovic. Thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Please have a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And for the remainder of time, shall we proceed with the examination-in-chief of next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. He has been waiting for a long time. It would be nice if we could do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But it's evident he should remain over the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Mr. President, while we're waiting if I could also indicate to the Trial Chamber next week the testimony of President Milorad Dodik is actually fixed for Tuesday at 9.00 in the morning. So to the extent that we don't complete the witness on Monday, we will ask that his testimony be interpreted so that President Dodik can testify and then we will resume when he is finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I take it there's no position from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I think we have relied on -- or understood the need for certain witnesses to have fixed times and the necessity to work around those times.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honour, on -- just on the topic of the document we were just discussing, I understand from my colleagues that it is -- maybe a reproduction of D2768. So perhaps the Defence can -- which is currently MFI'd. I think a translation has come through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat that? Actually I didn't follow.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: The document that we were just discussing appears to be a reproduction of MFI D2768.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you mean the leaflet?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll check it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Skoko.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skoko. Please be seated and make yourself comfortable. Yes, please proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Dr. Skoko.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SKOKO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to the gentlemen and the ladies of the Prosecution and of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Dr. Skoko, did you provide a statement to the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SKOKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have in e-court 1D07983. 1D07983.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Skoko, kindly look at the screen before you. Do you see the statement you provided to the Defence on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SKOKO
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Kindly pause until the interpretation of my questions is complete. Did you sign and read the statement?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SKOKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown the last page so that he can identify his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SKOKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the statement faithfully reflect your words?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SKOKO
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I were to put the same questions to you today, would your answers be the same, in essence?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SKOKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this package under 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. There are five associated exhibits that we are offering. We would ask that they all be added to our 65 ter list as we hadn't interviewed the witness at the time that list was filed. In addition, Mr. President, we're not going to be tendering the three additional exhibits, and we therefore will redact paragraphs 28 and 29 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Ms. Sutherland. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. We have no objection to the additional exhibits but we note that the provenance is unclear from the documents and the statements, and so we would have no objection if the Defence would elicit from the witness how the map was produced or who produced the map. The maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You -- you -- you mean the four maps referred to as associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As to the provenance.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It simply says a map showing data between 1992 and 1995. But it doesn't actually say who produced the map and it is unclear from the witness's statement whether he produced the map or he got it from somebody else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Fair enough. I think Mr. Karadzic can do that. Yes, shall we give the numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the 92 ter statement 1D7983 will be Exhibit D3321, and the five associated exhibits will be Exhibits D3322 through to D3326.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will read out a brief summary of Dr. Milorad Skoko's statement in the English language. [In English] Dr. Milorad Skoko was born on 15th of January, 1945, in Jugovici village, Gacko municipality, Bosnia-Herzegovina and now Republika Srpska. On 21st of December, 1991, the Ministerial Council was formed in response to the unconstitutional and unlawful conduct of the leadership of the SDA and HDZ. Dr. Milorad Skoko was appointed as a minister without a portfolio. On 1st of August, 1992, Dr. Milorad Skoko was appointed as general director of the Republika Srpska electric Supply Board. The electric power system of the former Yugoslavia collapsed first because of the war operations in Croatia in 1991 and later because of war operations in B and H in 1992. Almost all power transmission lines were damaged and the supply of electricity to utmost all areas in B and H was prevented. This prevented normal production of electricity in B and H power plants, reducing production capacity by 75 per cent which had a direct impact on the supply of Sarajevo. Of the remaining 25 percent of total power, 40 per cent was produced in the territory under the control of the VRS and 60 per cent was produced in the areas under control of the BH Army and HVO, military formation. At the beginning of the war, parts of both Serbian and Muslim Sarajevo experienced an irregular supply of electricity because of power network failure. There were never deliberate cuts of power supply to Sarajevo from the Serb side. Interruptions occurred when transmissions and distribution lines were damaged because of war operations. From 1992 to 1995, over 550 million kilowatt hours of electricity was supplied to the area of Sarajevo which was under the control of the BH Army. There were great distributions in the supply of power from the Visegrad hydropower plant to Sarajevo because of failures deliberately caused by members of BH Army who sabotaged power transmission lines. Throughout the conflict, Sarajevo did receive power from a small grid on the water-pipe line from Sarajevo, and from a power transmission lines and cable laid under Sarajevo airport. All other came through the Serbian territory. Considering this, and the fact that industrial production had almost completely stopped, the population was able to be supplied with sufficient electricity. The amount of electricity received allowed households in the federal Sarajevo to satisfy basic household needs. The supply of electricity to the people of federal Sarajevo during the war was not a power supply disaster, as the Muslims and world media -- Muslims and world media often portrayed it. Dr. Milorad Skoko was not aware of any sabotage, destruction of pylons or any other interference with the transmission system taking place in the territory of Republika Srpska. Failures mostly occurred in the territory of BH Federation. Discussions between Elektroprenos, this means electro transmission, and the BH Federation took place in the presence of the UNPROFOR representatives, and the necessary repairs and restoration of damaged transmissions -- transmission lines were carried out. There were never any decisions, orders, or instructions to cut off power supply to federal Sarajevo from the Serb side. Nobody from the Republika Srpska ever obstructed the power supplies to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to lead live on a particular document. Can we have 1D10082.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Skoko, did you have knowledge or an overview of the amount of electricity delivered to the other side during the war in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SKOKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, first of all, all of the four schematics that have been attached to the documentation for the Tribunal today as well as another document which confirms that in the less than four years of war Sarajevo received 550 million kilowatts of electricity were provided by the Elektroprenos of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Nowadays it is a unified institution at the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina. In other words, these documents were received from a BiH institution and its commission, as you can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you look at the table and tell us what it represents.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SKOKO
utterances.text: The table shown indicates the distribution of electricity per year delivered to the Muslim part of Sarajevo. That is to say, the part of Sarajevo that had allegedly been under complete energy blockade. I need to correct myself. I didn't say that there were no problems in the delivery of electricity but there was enough electricity for basic needs. What I assert is true is that when we take the total electricity and its amount divided over 45 months of the siege of Sarajevo, one easily calculates that every household received some 308 kilowatt hours of electricity. Nowadays in Serbia and many poor countries, 350 kilowatts of energy is considered the minimum level to satisfy basic human needs. I cannot discuss whether that electricity was used to this or that end. It is simply a fact of how much electricity was delivered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If it was used to this or that end, or to produce weapons or something similar, how did that reflect on the supply of households?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SKOKO
utterances.text: In any case, the households simply did not receive the amount of electricity used for other purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I wanted to ask you this. The map of the electricity system of Bosnia in 1991, what is the provenance and who created it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness needs to re-start his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Dr. Skoko, could you repeat your answer. Please -- please put a pause before you start answering the question because we have to hear the interpretation of Mr. Karadzic's question. Yes, could you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. All of the four maps provided as attachments to this -- to the documents, as well as the total of 550 million kilowatt hours is something that was put together by the Elektroprenos of BiH which is a unified institution of the Federation and the RS. Production is separate, distribution is separate, but Elektroprenos which is to say, distribution, is joint -- is a joint company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned a stamp. What document is it? It's the level -- or the report on the level of electricity supplied to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic kindly repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at -- well, can we have this document that's on the screen admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So it -- it's your evidence that this document we are seeing in front of us was also produced by Elektroprenos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3327, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D10078. It is attached to the maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell us what is this? Who drafted it? And who certified it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SKOKO
utterances.text: That is the document I just mentioned. It states that the -- that federal Sarajevo, that is to say, the Muslim part of Sarajevo, during the period in time, between 1992 and 1995, received 550 million kilowatt hours of electricity. This document was provided by Elektroprenos of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which is a unified institution at BiH level. They certified it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If this is not part of the associated exhibits, I tender it, and, for the time being, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it is. And --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit D3326 now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Dr. Skoko, as you have noted, your evidence in-chief in this case has, in most part, been submitted in writing, that is through your statement. And now you will be cross-examined by the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor, but given the time, we'll adjourn for today. So can I advise you, while you are staying over the weekend at The Hague. You are not supposed to discuss with anyone else about your testimony. Do you understand that, doctor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Finally, I would like the parties to check D2768, referred to by Ms. McKenna, and come back to the Chamber whether it is, indeed, the identical with the leaflet we dealt with. I'm not sure about it. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only wanted to have a few minutes on Monday to ask about some studies that were not admitted. Perhaps I won't even need to tender them, but I wanted to have something confirmed with the witness and put a few questions only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There's no difficulty with it. Hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
